'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Kyiv offensive (2022)|Kyiv offensive]]
****[[Battle of Kyiv (2022)|Battle of Kyiv]]
*****The [[Ukrainian Air Force]] says that it has destroyed two [[Russian Air Force|Russian]] warplanes in a [[dogfight]] over [[Kyiv]]. A Ukrainian [[Mikoyan MiG-29|MiG-29]] is also shot down during the air battle. [https://news.sky.com/story/ukraine-invasion-paratroopers-storm-military-hospital-in-kharkiv-overnight-as-russian-forces-close-in-on-kyiv-12555332 (Sky News)]
***[[Kherson offensive]]
****[[Battle of Kherson]]
*****[[Russian Ground Forces]] say that they have captured the [[Black Sea]] port of [[Kherson]]. The [[Ministry of Defence (Ukraine)|Ukrainian Ministry of Defense]] denies this claim, stating that the battle is ongoing. [https://edition.cnn.com/europe/live-news/ukraine-russia-putin-news-03-02-22/h_94fb56edc8c774021fe635cda015d2fd (CNN)]
*****The mayor of Kherson says that the city has fallen to the invading Russian forces. [https://www.nytimes.com/live/2022/03/02/world/ukraine-russia-war#the-strategic-city-of-kherson-in-ukraines-south-falls-to-russian-forces (''The New York Times'')]
****[[Siege of Mariupol]]
*****The mayor of [[Mariupol]] reports mass casualties and a water outage from "non-stop" Russian bombardments. [https://www.reuters.com/world/mariupol-mayor-reports-mass-casualties-nonstop-russian-attack-2022-03-02/ (Reuters)]
***[[Horlivka offensive]]
****Ukrainian forces begin an offensive towards [[Horlivka]]. [https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-ato/3417782-ukrainian-servicemen-inflict-serious-damage-on-enemy-in-horlivka.html (Ukrinform)]
***[[Siege of Chernihiv]]
****Two [[3M-54 Kalibr|Kalibr]] [[cruise missiles]] strike a [[Healthcare in Ukraine|hospital]] in [[Chernihiv]] after Russian troops were forced to retreat. [https://time.com/6153790/russia-ukraine-more-talks/ (TIME)] [https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/ukraine-russia-invasion-mar2-2022-1.6369595 (CBC)]
***[[Battle of Kharkiv (2022)|Battle of Kharkiv]]
****Russian forces launch [[airstrike]]s on [[Kharkiv National University]] and a local police department. [https://www.cnn.com/2022/03/02/europe/ukraine-russia-invasion-wednesday-intl-hnk/index.html (CNN)]
***[[Siege of Enerhodar]]
****Russia says that its troops have captured the [[Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant]], the largest [[nuclear power plant]] in Europe. The [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] confirms that Russia had communicated that the plant was under their control and that personnel at the plant were continuing to perform their normal duties. [https://www.thedrive.com/the-war-zone/44534/russia-says-its-forces-in-ukraine-have-captured-europes-largest-nuclear-power-plant (The Drive)]
***A missile strikes the [[Bangladesh]]i-flagged cargo ship ''Banglar Samriddhi'' docked at the Port of Olvia in [[Mykolaiv Oblast]], killing a Bangladeshi engineer. [https://www.thedailystar.net/news/world/2022-russian-invasion-ukraine/news/bangladeshi-sailor-killed-missile-attack-ukraine-2974366 (''The Daily Star'')]
***[[Eleventh emergency special session of the United Nations General Assembly|An emergency special session]] of the [[United Nations General Assembly|UN General Assembly]] adopts a resolution calling for Russia to end the invasion. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/un-assembly-to-vote-on-resolution-demanding-russia-stop-war/2022/03/02/d29ecbfa-99e5-11ec-9987-9dceee62a3f6_story.html (''The Washington Post'')] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/mar/02/united-nations-russia-ukraine-vote (''The Guardian'')]
***In an unprecedented move, the [[European Court of Human Rights]] (ECHR) suspends all judicial proceedings against Ukraine pending before the ECHR. [https://www.eurointegration.com.ua/news/2022/03/2/7135092/ (''Europeiska Pravda'')] 
***The [[Ukrainian Armed Forces]] say that Ukraine has retaken the city of [[Makariv]] from Russia. [https://www.jpost.com/international/article-699106 (''Jerusalem Post'')] [https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-ato/3418214-ukraines-armed-forces-regain-control-of-makariv-near-kyiv.html (Ukrinform)]
*[[Papua conflict]]
**[[Telkomsel shooting]]
***Members of the [[Free Papua Movement]] gun down eight people at a [[Telkomsel]] telecommunications tower in [[Puncak Regency]], [[West Papua (province)|West Papua]]. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2022-03-04/separatists-in-indonesias-papua-kill-8-workers-at-telecom-tower (U.S. News & World Report)]
*[[Anglophone crisis]]
**Anglophone rebels bomb a car in the [[Ekondo-Titi]] [[communes of Cameroon|commune]] of [[Southwest Region (Cameroon)|Southwest]] [[Cameroon]], killing seven people, including the mayor and a [[lieutenant]]. [https://www.voanews.com/a/cameroon-says-rebel-bomb-kills-officials/6468320.html (VOA)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[2022 Russian financial crisis]]
**The [[European Union]] removes seven [[Russia]]n banks from the [[SWIFT]] financial messaging system, including [[VTB Bank]], [[Novikombank]], [[Promsvyazbank]], [[Rossiya Bank]], [[Sovcombank]] and [[VEB.RF]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/eu-excludes-seven-russian-banks-swift-official-journal-2022-03-02/ (Reuters)]
**Russian stocks endure a total wipeout in value on the [[London stock exchange]], losing [[United States dollar|$]]570 billion in two weeks, with many Russian companies' stocks [[penny stock|worth pennies]]. Entities such as [[Gazprom]] and [[Lukoil]] have lost almost all of their value. [[Sberbank]], the largest bank in Russia, had a [[market cap]] of $102 billion six months ago but the value of outstanding shares is currently less than $190 million. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-03-02/london-listed-russian-stocks-erase-570-billion-in-two-weeks?srnd=premium-europe (Bloomberg)] [https://www.barrons.com/articles/russian-stocks-ukraine-sanctions-51646241831 (''Barron's'')]
**The [[World Bank]] suspends all programs in Russia and Belarus in response to [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|the invasion of Ukraine]]. [https://labs.letemps.ch/chat/custom/guerre-russie-ukraine-b/index.php (''Le Temps'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Four people are suffocated to death in [[Pune district]], [[India]], after being given the task to clean out a septic tank. [https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/other-states/four-die-of-suffocation-while-cleaning-septic-tank-in-pune-district/article65183374.ece (The Hindu)] 
*A [[Romanian Air Force]] [[MiG-21]] from the [[RoAF 86th Air Base|86th Air Base]], which was carrying out an air patrol mission over [[Dobruja]], vanishes from radar, and an [[IAR 330]] rescue helicopter sent on a [[search and rescue]] mission also disappears. A Defence Ministry spokesman later confirms that the helicopter crashed near [[Gura Dobrogei]], killing all seven crew members on board. The fate of the MiG-21 and its pilot is still unknown. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/five-dead-romanian-military-rescue-helicopter-crash-defence-ministry-2022-03-02/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong]]
****[[Hong Kong]] reports a record 55,353 new [[COVID-19]] cases and 160 deaths in the past 24 hours. [https://news.rthk.hk/rthk/en/component/k2/1636773-20220302.htm (RTHK)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] surpasses 200,000 daily cases from COVID-19 for the first time after reporting a record 219,241 new cases. [https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20220302002200320 (Yonhap News Agency)]
****[[Prime Minister of South Korea|South Korean Prime Minister]] [[Kim Boo-kyum]] tests positive for COVID-19. [http://www.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=20220303000154 (''Korea Herald'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****[[Spain]] surpasses 100,000 deaths from COVID-19. [https://www.abc.es/sociedad/abci-espana-alcanza-100000-muertos-covid-19-segun-sanidad-202203021914_noticia.html (ABC.es)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[Turkey]] eases the majority of its COVID-19-related restrictions including easing of [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|mask mandate]] indoors and outdoors and no longer asking [[contact tracing]] when entering public places two years after the first COVID-19 cases in the country. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/turkey-eases-coronavirus-related-restrictions-minister-2022-03-02/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in Australia]]
****The [[Australian Technical Advisory Group on Immunisation]] recommends the usage of the [[Novavax COVID-19 vaccine]] as a booster dose. [https://www.skynews.com.au/world-news/novavax-vaccine-recommended-for-use-as-a-covid19-booster-by-atagi-for-australians-aged-over-18-where-mrna-jab-is-not-suitable/news-story/4feeac1c71c79a333eb25f35e3458b91?amp (Sky News Australia)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***A study published by the ''[[The New England Journal of Medicine|New England Journal of Medicine]]'' shows that the booster shot of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]] restores protection against the [[SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant|Omicron variant]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/amp/rcna18281 (NBC News)]
**[[COVID-19 drug development]]
***A [[World Health Organization]] (WHO) panel of International experts recommends the use of [[Merck & Co.]]'s COVID-19 [[Antiviral drug|antiviral pill]] [[Molnupiravir]] for high-risk patients. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-03-02/merck-s-covid-antiviral-gets-who-backing-for-high-risk-patients (Bloomberg)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Reactions to the 2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis]], [[International reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Russia–Ukraine relations]]
***Ceasefire talks between Russia and Ukraine, scheduled to take place today, are postponed. [https://tass.ru/politika/13927423 (TASS)]
***The Russian delegation arrives in [[Belarus]] for a second round of talks expected to occur on Thursday morning. [https://www.cnn.com/europe/live-news/ukraine-russia-putin-news-03-02-22/index.html (CNN)] [https://news.am/eng/news/689525.html#.Yh-qJWeu4l8.twitter (News.am)]
**[[Russia–Turkey relations]]
***[[Turkey]] says that the [[Russian Navy]] has cancelled the transit of four of its warships through the [[Bosporus]] strait upon request after Turkey triggered the wartime clause of the [[Montreux Convention Regarding the Regime of the Straits]], which allows Turkey to close the Bosporus strait and the [[Dardanelles]] to foreign warships. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/turkey-says-russia-cancelled-black-sea-passage-bid-upon-its-request-2022-03-02/ (Reuters)]
**[[Russia–European Union relations]]
***The European Union will suspend deliveries of [[euro]] [[banknotes of the euro|banknotes]] to Russia beginning on March 12, with exemptions for private persons and their family members in Russia as well as diplomatic missions with legal immunity. [https://tass.com/politics/1415193 (TASS)]
**[[Russia–United States relations]]
***[[Assistant to the Secretary of Defense for Public Affairs|Pentagon Press Secretary]] [[John Kirby (admiral)|John Kirby]] announces that the [[United States|U.S.]] will postpone a [[LGM-30 Minuteman|Minuteman III]] [[Intercontinental ballistic missile|ICBM]] missile test in an effort to de-escalate tensions between Russia and Ukraine. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-delays-icbm-test-launch-bid-de-escalate-russia-nuclear-tensions-2022-03-02/ (Reuters)]
**[[Germany–Russia relations]]
***[[Germany]] seizes [[Alisher Usmanov]]'s [[superyacht]] [[Dilbar (yacht)|''Dilbar'']] in [[Hamburg]] after the [[Russian oligarch]] was [[International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War|sanctioned]] by the EU on Monday. [https://www.forbes.com/sites/giacomotognini/2022/03/02/germans-seize-russian-billionaire-alisher-usmanovs-mega-yacht/?sh=746f7a6a52dd (Forbes)]
**[[China–Russia relations]]
***A Western intelligence report indicates that [[China]] had some level of knowledge about the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|Russian invasion of Ukraine]] as it requested Russian officials not to invade during the [[2022 Olympic Games]]. China disputes the accuracy of the reports, saying they are a way to shift blame on the country and smear it. [https://www.nytimes.com/2022/03/02/us/politics/russia-ukraine-china.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[Nuclear program of Iran]]
**During a meeting in [[Israel]], [[Chancellor of Germany|German Chancellor]] [[Olaf Scholz]] says that a new agreement to revive the [[Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action]] "cannot be postponed any longer". However, [[Prime Minister of Israel|Prime Minister]] [[Naftali Bennett]] calls the agreement "unacceptable" as he indicated that [[Iran]] would be allowed to install centrifuges on a large scale. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/scholz-says-iran-deal-must-be-reached-now-bennett-calls-renewed-pact-unacceptable/amp/ (''Times of Israel'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Protests against responses to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 anti-lockdown protests in New Zealand]]
***Anti-lockdown rioters clash with police at the [[New Zealand Parliament Buildings]] in [[Wellington]]. A fire breaks out, destroying a [[playground|children's playground]]. Several police officers are injured and 38 protesters are arrested. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/mar/02/police-move-to-clear-new-zealand-protests-as-maori-king-calls-for-end-to-occupation (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/health/coronavirus/300529966/full-coverage-police-operation-ends-parliament-occupation (Stuff)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[Protests against the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Opposition to Vladimir Putin in Russia|Russian Opposition Leader]] [[Alexei Navalny]] calls for more [[Anti-war movement|anti-war protests]] [[2022 anti-war protests in Russia|in Russia]] and across the world, as well as protests against [[President of Russia|President]] [[Vladimir Putin]]. [https://thehill.com/policy/international/596522-navalny-calls-for-protests-in-russia-calls-putin-an-obviously-insane?amp (''The Hill'')]
**The [[International Criminal Court]] announces that they have opened a criminal investigation into [[war crime]]s that have been committed in [[Ukraine]] since 2013, including [[War crimes during the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|during the invasion]]. [https://www.businessinsider.com/ukraine-international-criminal-court-begins-war-crimes-investigation-2022-3 (''Business Insider'')]
*[[2021–2022 Myanmar insurgency]]
**The [[Chairman of the State Administration Council|Myanmar military junta]] pardons several celebrities who spoke out against [[2021 Myanmar coup d'état|the military coup]] including [[Lu Min (actor)|Lu Min]], [[Wyne (film director)|Wyne]], [[Pyay Ti Oo]], [[Eaindra Kyaw Zin]] and [[Paing Takhon]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/amp/Entertainment/wireStory/myanmar-pardons-celebrities-jailed-anti-military-views-83201840 (ABC News)]
*Hundreds of women protest in the [[Nigeria]]n capital of [[Abuja]] after the [[National Assembly (Nigeria)|National Assembly]] rejected a series of amendments to the [[Constitution of Nigeria|Constitution]] that would have expanded [[women's rights]] and [[autonomy]]. The proposed amendments included reserving 35% of all legislative seats and [[political parties in Nigeria|political party]] leadership positions for women, conferred [[Nigerian nationality law|citizenship]] to foreign husbands of Nigerian women, and allowing women to inherit the ancestry of their husband after five years of marriage. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/3/2/nigerian-women-protest-parliament-rejection-of-pro-equality-bills (Al Jazeera)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Censorship of Wikipedia]], [[Media freedom in Russia]]
**Russia's communications regulator, [[Roskomnadzor]], threatens to block the [[Russian Wikipedia]] for hosting an article on the [[w:ru:Вторжение России на Украину (2022)|Russian invasion of Ukraine]], which the regulator alleges to be factually inaccurate. The same concerns the Russian edition of US-sponsored [[Voice of America]] (VOA); [[Current Time TV]] (a joint publication of [[Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty]] and VOA) is already reported to be blocked in the country. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/moscow-threatens-block-russian-language-wikipedia-over-invasion-article-2022-03-02/ (Reuters)] [https://www.axios.com/russia-threatens-block-voa-removes-ukraine-invasion-coverage-cb1a930b-87b9-460f-8ac6-08a02b670ccc.html (Axios)]
*[[OneWeb satellite constellation]]
**Russian [[List of government space agencies|space agency]] [[Roscosmos]] says that it will not launch 36 [[OneWeb]] [[satellite]]s from the [[Baikonur Cosmodrome]] on Friday, unless OneWeb provides "legally binding guarantees" that the satellites will not be used for military purposes by the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-60587154 (BBC News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2022 Winter Paralympics]]
**The [[International Paralympic Committee]] bans [[Russia]] and [[Belarus]] from competing in the upcoming [[Winter Paralympics]] in [[Beijing]] after initially announcing they would compete despite the invasion of Ukraine, taking part as "neutral countries".  [https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/winter-olympics/paralympics-russia-belarus-athletes-news-b2026684.html?amp (''The Independent'')] [https://www.axios.com/ioc-russia-belarus-beijing-paralympics-ban-c400fe48-c14f-4aac-86a1-8608213a3549.html (Axios)]
